newsitem.title: LATVIA: MPS AGAIN REJECT SECURITIES WATCHDOG CANDIDATES.
newsitem.headline: MPS AGAIN REJECT SECURITIES WATCHDOG CANDIDATES.

text.p: Parliament has again rejected all three new candidates for remaining posts on the board of stock market watchdog the securities commission, the budget and finance committe said on Thursday.
"The parliament vote was negative for all the three names suggested by the securities commission," a parliament budget commission spokeswoman told Reuters.
"Tomorrow I will suggest a new set of candidates," securities commission chairman Viktors Gustsons said.
"I will just have to come up with more experience, bigger names," he added.
Parliament rejected Janis Brazovskis, a central bank official, Andris Miglavs, an economist, and Pauls Dzintars Kalninsh from a U.S. based consultancy.
This is the second time MPs have rejected candidates proposed by the commission, a state watchdog of the financial markets, which started work early this year.

"Good securities professionals are not numerous in this country and anti-corruption law makes the picking-and-choosing more difficult," Gustsons said, noting he originally intended to have the board in place already in February.
